lines: Node-based sequencer of sixteen nodes joined by arrows printed on the panel, each node carrying up to four CV sliders, with a different arrangement of arrows, sliders and modifiers each week
Sets the CV that step of the node plays, giving the voltage of the low -/+ knob at the bottom of its travel and the high knob at the top; a node takes four clock pulses, shared between its sliders
Turns this configuration's global modifier on and off, the same switch that playing the node carrying that modifier flips
Triggers a reset every so many node transitions, 1 to 64; at the top of its travel no internal reset happens, which the panel marks OFF and the tooltip prints as Infinty
Sets which column a reset jumps to: Col 1, Col 2, Col 3 or Col 4 by number, or Current Col, Next Col, Previous Col or Random Col
Sets which of this configuration's arrows are active: No Arrows, Left Arrows or All Arrows
Sets the voltage the bottom of every slider's travel gives, -10V to 10V
Sets the voltage the top of every slider's travel gives, -10V to 10V
A rising edge moves the sequencer on one step, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V
A rising edge resets the sequencer to the column the COL knob names, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V
A rising edge plays that node, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V; patch it from another node's output or from an external gate
Carries 10V while a node is playing, and one channel per node playing at once, up to four, when the configuration runs more than one at a time
Carries the CV of the step being played, scaled between the two -/+ knobs and passed through the built-in quantizer, with one channel per node playing at once, up to four
Carries 10V when that node finishes and the branch through this jack is the one taken; patch it to the input of another node to add a connection of your own
Note — The arrangement of arrows, sliders and modifiers is a configuration, and a new one is published weekly. A module keeps the one it was made with until This Week's Config is used on its menu.
Note — What a modifier icon does is written in its own tooltip, so turn tooltips on in Rack's settings and hover the icon to read it.
Note — A node reached with no active arrow and no patch cable out of it triggers a reset.
Note — Bypassing this module leaves every output at 0V.
Menu — Quantizer — a submenu setting the scale and root note the CV output is quantized to
Menu — Randomize CVs — rolls a new value for every slider on every node
Menu — This Week's Config — replaces this module's configuration with the one published for the current week
Menu — Open Config Collection — opens a browser of every configuration this rack has used, where one can be chosen, marked a favourite or filtered by the modifiers it carries
Menu — Random Config from Collection — switches to a configuration picked at random from that collection
Menu — Slider Light Settings — a submenu holding the two settings that change how a slider's lit part is drawn
Menu — Bidirectional — on the Slider Light Settings submenu; lights a slider from the middle of its track out to the handle rather than from the bottom up
Menu — Full On — on the Slider Light Settings submenu; lights the whole of a slider's track rather than only the part below the handle

GlassShard.notes: No source is published for this plugin, so everything here was read from the installed binary, version 2.0.1, which is unstripped and carries one GlassShard::process. The maker's manual at PathSetManuals was read alongside it and agrees with the code everywhere it was checked. Param ranges come from the constructor: Reset Count 1 to 65 with a default of 8 (0xc05c), Reset Column a switch of 0 to 7 with the labels Col 1, Col 2, Col 3, Col 4, Current Col, Next Col, Previous Col, Random Col (0xc270), Arrow Intensity a switch of 1 to 3 with the labels No Arrows, Left Arrows, All Arrows and a default of 2 (0xc444), Lowest CV -10 to 10 defaulting to -3 (0xc520) and Highest CV -10 to 10 defaulting to 3 (0xc590). Each slider is a CVQuantity running 0 to 1 with a default of 0.5, whose displayed value is lowest + value × (highest − lowest) quantized (0xe5f0). At the top of Reset Count the tooltip reads Infinty, a spelling mistake in the binary at 0xe97c; the panel prints OFF under the knob. The maker's convention holds here: every trigger jack on the module, clock, reset and the sixteen node inputs alike, is a Schmitt trigger taking high at 2V and low at 0.1V. The other half of that convention does not apply, since GlassShard has no knob-plus-attenuverter CV inputs at all. Two of the three Toggle Global Effect params, 65 and 66, have no widget position and no click can reach them, so they are left untagged; only param 64 is placed on the panel. The census gives every node input the same position and every slider of a given number the same position, because those widgets are children of a per-node container rather than of the panel; the tags are by index and are unaffected, but a position-based lookup will not tell nodes apart. The number and placement of sliders, arrows and modifiers changes with each weekly configuration, so no line here names a particular modifier. check_numbers.py reports the 0.1V trigger floor as absent from the binary; it is absent as a stored constant only, because the compiler materialises 0x3DCCCCCD with a mov/movk pair inside the instruction stream (0xda0c, 0xdbc8, 0xd680) rather than loading it from a literal pool. The 2V threshold is an fmov immediate for the same reason.
